newsitem.title: MADAGASCAR: Madagascar president flies to the United States.
newsitem.headline: Madagascar president flies to the United States.

text.p: Madagascar's new President Didier Ratsiraka left on Thursday for the United States to assure the International Monetary Fund of his commitment to terms of an aid package.

Ratsiraka, a 60-year old retired admiral elected president in December, and his large delegation would also visit Brussels and Paris for talks with European Commission President Jacques Santer and French President Jacques Chirac, officials said.

They said Ratsiraka, military ruler of Madagascar for 18 years before being voted out in 1993, would meet IMF managing-director Michel Camdessus in Washington to discuss the release of a second tranche of an Enhanced Structural Adjustment Facility package of loans for the vast Indian Ocean island.
Camdessus urged Ratsiraka on his election as president of one of the world's poorest countries to pursue "healthy" financial policies. Madagascar has a foreign debt of some $4 billion.
Ratsiraka's predecessor, Albert Zafy, relied on "parallel financing" -- private loans ostensibly for development projects but at higher interest rates than from multilateral donors such as the IMF.
On a visit to Madagascar last year Camdessus said he was shocked by the island's economic decline since 1991.
